title: finding(types): `@object-ui/types` has no `test` script, so `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types run test` exits 0 having run nothing
body:
## Observation

`packages/types/package.json` declares `build`, `clean`, `type-check`, `lint` — and no `test`. `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types run test` therefore matches zero scripts and **exits 0 with no output**: it reads as a pass, and nothing ran.

The package is not untested. It carries 147 test files and 2811 tests, but they run only through the ROOT vitest config (`pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/`), which is how CI reaches them. So the two spellings a contributor might reasonably reach for diverge silently:

    pnpm --filter @object-ui/types run test        exit 0, 0 tests run, no output
    pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/           exit 0, 147 files, 2811 tests

Measured on `origin/main` @ `1cca4415e`, while working objectui#8361 (PR #8589). This seat hit it: a verification step of the form `type-check && test` returned exit 0 and printed only the `type-check` banner, and the missing half was visible only because the vitest summary lines were absent from the log.

## Class size

Measured on the same tree, over `packages/*/package.json` and `apps/*/package.json`: **42 workspace manifests, 38 declare a `test` script, 4 do not.** So the majority spelling exists and this is an asymmetry within the repo, not a house style. (The other three are not enumerated here — that is the triage seat's call, along with whether they are in the same situation or genuinely have nothing to run.)

## Why this is worth a card and not a shrug

The failure mode is a silent green in a verification step, which is the shape that costs a reader their trust in every other green in the same log. It is the same family as objectui#8361 itself — an instrument that reports "nothing to report" when what happened is "nothing was measured" — but a completely different mechanism, and it is not fixed by that card.

## Options (not a ruling — filed for triage)

- A. Add `"test": "vitest run --config ../../vitest.config.mts packages/types"` (or whatever spelling the root config wants) to the four manifests, so the per-package spelling reaches the tests that already exist.
- B. Leave the manifests alone and make the ABSENCE loud instead — a gate asserting every workspace package that owns test files also declares a `test` script.
- C. Leave it: CI runs the root config and is correct; the cost is local, and lands on whoever types the per-package spelling.

Observation-class finding (`finding` label, no `pm:queue`): nothing ships wrong and CI's verdict is correct; the cost is a misleading local green.

Filed from Claude Code session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr` while working objectui#8361 (PR #8589).
